title: Handling of Empty Log Set Retrieval
description: Verify that the API gracefully handles requests for log data within a time range where no events have occurred, ensuring proper structure and status code.
preconditions: A specific date range is defined (e.g., 2099-12-31 to 2100-01-01) known to contain zero audit entries.
steps: 1. Send GET request to /audit/logs specifying the empty time range.
2. Verify the response status code is 200 OK.
3. Validate that the response body contains an empty array or a specific 'no records found' message, without throwing an error.
expected_result: The API returns a successful 200 OK status code with a structured payload indicating zero results (e.g., {'logs': [], 'count': 0}). No server errors should occur.
requirement: Get all endpoints and make sure none repeats or has lose ends

title: Unauthorized Access Attempt on Audit Logs Endpoint
description: Validate that only users with 'Administrator' or specific 'Audit Viewer' roles can access the audit logs endpoint. Attempts by unauthenticated or low-privilege users must be rejected.
preconditions: A user account with insufficient permissions (e.g., standard user) exists.
steps: 1. Attempt GET request to /audit/logs using an unauthenticated token.
2. Repeat step 1 using a valid token belonging to a non-admin, low-privilege role.
expected_result: The API must return a 403 Forbidden status code for all unauthorized attempts, and the response body should clearly indicate insufficient permissions.
requirement: Get all endpoints and make sure none repeats or has lose ends

title: Verify Global Security Headers and Rate Limiting Enforcement
description: This test validates that the API enforces necessary security headers (CORS, HSTS) and correctly implements rate limiting mechanisms across all endpoints.
preconditions: The API service must be running at http://localhost:8000/docs
A valid client IP address is used for testing.
steps: Step 1: Send GET /status with no body and header Accept: application/json (Initial request)
Step 2: Assert status code 200
Step 3: Verify response headers include 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*' or specific allowed origins.
Step 4: Send GET /users with no body and header Accept: application/json (Repeated request)
Step 5: Assert status code 429 Too Many Requests after exceeding the defined rate limit threshold.
Step 6: Verify response headers include 'X-RateLimit-Remaining' and 'Retry-After'.
expected_result: The API returns correct security CORS headers, enforces rate limiting (HTTP 429), and provides necessary header information for client handling.
requirement: Get all endpoints and make sure none repeats or has lose ends

title: Validate API Surface for Injection Vulnerabilities Across All Endpoints
description: This test systematically checks common endpoints for injection vulnerabilities by passing malicious payloads (e.g., SQL, XSS) in parameters and bodies, ensuring proper sanitization.
preconditions: The API service must be running at http://localhost:8000/docs
A set of valid test credentials (if applicable) are available.
steps: Step 1: Send GET /users?q=<script>alert(1)</script> with no body and header Accept: application/json
Step 2: Assert status code 200 or 400 (indicating rejection of malicious input)
Step 3: Verify response does not execute scripts or return database errors.
Step 4: Send POST /products with body {"name": "Test Product", "description": "<script>alert(1)</script>"} and header Content-Type: application/json
Step 5: Assert status code 201 (or appropriate success code)
Step 6: Verify response payload sanitizes the malicious input in the 'description' field.
expected_result: All endpoints successfully reject or sanitize common injection payloads, preventing unauthorized data access or execution.
requirement: Get all endpoints and make sure none repeats or has lose ends

title: Stress Test: Concurrent Endpoint Health Check Validation
description: Simulates concurrent requests to validate the health and availability of multiple endpoints simultaneously, ensuring no service degradation or rate limiting issues.
preconditions: The API service must be running at http://localhost:8000/docs
Concurrency testing tool (e.g., JMeter, Locust) is configured.
steps: Step 1: Send concurrent GET requests to a defined list of core endpoints (e.g., /users, /products, /status).
Step 2: Assert that all simultaneous requests receive status code 200 within the specified concurrency window.
Step 3: Monitor response time variance across all concurrent calls; standard deviation must be low.
Step 4: Verify that no endpoint returns a 'lose ends' or internal server error (5xx) under load.
expected_result: All targeted endpoints remain highly available and responsive when subjected to high concurrency, confirming system stability.
requirement: Get all endpoints and make sure none repeats or has lose ends

title: Performance Test: Comprehensive Endpoint Discovery and Validation

preconditions: The API service must be running at http://localhost:8000/docs
A sufficient volume of mock endpoints must be available for testing payload size.

Step 2: Assert status code 200
Step 3: Verify response time is less than 500ms (Performance Threshold)
Step 4: Verify the response payload size is within acceptable limits (e.g., < 1MB for initial discovery).
Step 5: Assert that all returned endpoint definitions are unique and do not contain 'lose ends' (i.e., all required parameters/paths are defined).
expected_result: The API successfully returns a comprehensive, non-redundant list of endpoints within acceptable performance thresholds.
requirement: Get all endpoints and make sure none repeats or has lose ends
